newsitem.title: USA: Tucson Electric seeks to cut rates 1.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Tucson Electric seeks to cut rates 1.1 pct.

text.p: Tucson Electric Power Co filed Wednesday with the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) for an across-the-board price reduction of $6.8 million, or 1.1 percent, for retail customers.

"In preparation for a competitive market, TEP has implemented a number of cost containment efforts that have led to significant reductions in our company's operational costs," said Charles Bayless, TEP chief executive officer.
The company's rate cut request was filed approximately 15 months after TEP reached a rate settlement with the ACC authorizing a 1.1 percent price increase.

Under the terms of the March 1996 rate settlement, TEP committed to aggressively pursue opportunities to reduce prices through cost-containment, operational enhancements and organizational realignment.
Savings realized from these efforts would then be shared between the company and its retail customers.
TEP said cost savings were realized primarily from renegotiated fuel contracts and the company's voluntary severance program, which cut its workforce by about 15 percent.
